templates.text: Subtle asymmetry noted in the motor cortex, with slightly reduced sulcation on the left hemisphere.
Delayed myelination observed in the auditory radiations, correlating with a dampened acoustic startle response.
Focal cortical thinning in the prefrontal region, potentially impacting early self-regulation circuits.
A mild dysgenesis of the corpus callosum is present, suggesting possible interhemispheric transfer delays.
Diffuse white matter gliosis noted, which may underlie a generalized dampening of reflexive vigor.
Asymmetry in the brainstem auditory pathways, with right-sided responses lagging by {milliseconds} ms.
A small, isolated periventricular nodule is disrupting local white matter tracts for upper limb control.
The visual cortex shows delayed gyral patterning, which may affect early orienting to complex stimuli.
Pronounced thinning of the cerebellar vermis, likely contributing to subtle truncal hypotonia.
Myelination in the corticospinal tracts is patchy and uneven, particularly on the right side.
A discrete area of polymicrogyria in the temporal lobe may influence auditory processing specificity.
Reduced neuronal density in the basal ganglia, potentially modulating the intensity of spontaneous movement.
The acoustic cry reflex shows a consistent latency, hinting at a brainstem processing anomaly.
Mild ventriculomegaly with stretching of adjacent periventricular white matter pathways.
Anomalous sulcal depth in the sensorimotor strip, correlating with asymmetric palmar grasp strength.
Focal heterotopia identified near the central sulcus, disrupting typical sensorimotor mapping.
Delayed maturation of the frontal operculum, a region implicated in early social-orienting behaviors.
The auditory cortex demonstrates a blurred gray-white matter junction on neuroimaging.
A subtle schizencephaly cleft in the right parietal lobe affects somatosensory integration.
Myelination delay is most pronounced in the posterior limb of the internal capsule.
Cortical asymmetry extends to the planum temporale, a key site for phonetic discrimination.
A small arachnoid cyst over the left hemisphere is exerting mild mass effect on underlying cortex.
The acoustic startle shows a fragmented, two-phase motor pattern instead of a unified response.
Diffuse excessive high signal intensity in the white matter on T2-weighted sequences.
The corticobulbar tracts appear underdeveloped, which may moderate facial expressivity and cry vigor.
A focal area of pachygyria in the frontal lobe suggests disrupted neuronal migration timing.
The neonatal cry shows reduced harmonic complexity, consistent with subtle laryngeal control anomalies.
Asymmetric development of the hippocampal formations, with the right side notably smaller.
The visual evoked potential demonstrates a prolonged latency, indicating optic radiation immaturity.
A discrete perisylvian polymicrogyria may underlie emerging oral-motor coordination differences.
